reasons.agent: Developer (Sonnet) by default: most of this is well-specified UI work, where Sonnet's lower cost matters more than Opus's extra depth.
reasons.builder: Developer (Sonnet) builds every task that names no builder, for the same cost reason.
reasons.checker: QA (Opus) checks every task that names no checker, since checking is where a missed defect is cheapest to catch.
reasons.cron: Every five minutes, so a finished task is picked up for checking promptly.
reasons.mode: A flow: after the view exists, grouping-and-stats and the run entry points touch different files and can run in parallel.
reasons.stop: Stop when the queue empties; the slice is small and there is no reason to keep the flow firing.

design:
Settled in the mock the operator drove on 2026-11-02 (hub/ui/mock, `#traces`; components src/components/traces/TracesPage.tsx and tracesModel.ts, styles src/styles/traces.css, fixtures recorded read-only from the operator's Hub by mock/record_traces.py). The components are the deliverable: building this slice wires them to the Hub's routes rather than redrawing them.

- Placement: a fourth view of the Activity tab, beside Ledger, Activity and Logs (operator: 'lives inside Activity'). An own top-bar tab was shown beside it and not chosen.
- Filter row: agent and time range as selects on the left; on the right a quiet 'Hub internals' menu (worker calls, requests, background work, events, with counts, and 'Back to agent runs'). Task, conversation and run filters show as removable chips; a row's task or conversation is narrowed to from a small control that appears on the row's hover, so a click anywhere else on the row opens its trace instead of filtering by accident (found while driving the mock).
- Totals: three tiles, cost (with unpriced runs left out and counted), duration (total, average, still running) and errors (by why: failed, stopped, ended in error); one quieter line below with tokens, model calls, tool calls and time waiting on the operator.
- Grouping: a switch (None, Agent, Model, Task, Conversation, Day; Kind applies within Hub internals). Each group is a row with its count, cost with a bar for its share of the total, total and average time, errors, and 'Only this'; it expands to its runs.
- A row: started, agent, model, task (reference and title) or conversation (marked as a conversation turn), took, cost or 'unpriced' ('—' while running), outcome. A run still running is neither priced nor unpriced until it ends.
- Opening a row opens the existing trace drawer, now also usable controlled by the screen that lists runs (TraceDrawer); the drawer itself is unchanged.

checked: hub/ui/src/components/environment/TracesSection.tsx: the only trace list, in Project Settings, kind filter only, 10 rows per page.

Trace entry points on screen today, by searching every use of TraceButton: a conversation turn (AgentTimeline.tsx:489, by run), a run row in the task story inside the task detail drawer (TaskStory.tsx:344, by run), and the Settings list (TracesSection.tsx:129, by trace). ConversationBar.tsx:201 declares 'Trace of the last turn', but no caller passes onOpenTrace.

Screens that name or count runs with no trace link, by searching the UI for run references: EvidencePieces.tsx:107 ('still being recorded by run …'), SpecRetrospective.tsx:317 (transcripts read, by run id), TaskTransitionHistory.tsx, LoopTab.tsx:452 (loop firing history), JobDetails.tsx:30 (job firing dots), SpecBuilds.tsx:206 ('N runs'), activity/ProjectWork.tsx:61 ('N runs').
hub/hub/api/v1/traces.py:41-75: the list route filters by run_id, task_id, conversation_id and operation; no agent or time range; no aggregate route.
hub/ui/src/api/traces.ts:18-36: each listed trace carries agent, conversation, task, run status, start and end time, span count; no cost or tokens.

Read-only queries on the operator's :8000 database, 2026-11-02: run root spans (invoke_agent) carry agent, model, task, conversation, cost (aw.usage.api_equivalent_usd_micros), usage status and token counts as attributes; root operations are invoke_agent 1,170, chat (worker) 1,015, aw.request 20,438, aw.work 4,280, aw.event 342 (git commands are spans inside other traces, not traces of their own); runs table statuses completed 1,211, failed 12, stopped 5, running 3; 136,761 spans in total.

The mock (hub/ui/mock #traces), fed every run trace of the operator's Hub recorded read-only by mock/record_traces.py and driven by the operator on 2026-11-02: totals $734 over 1,170 runs, 16 finished runs unpriced, 17 errors (12 failed, 5 stopped); grouping by task showed six tasks that no longer exist and one task (VSCBE-4) with 311 runs. Typecheck (tsconfig.mock.json) and lint clean on the new files.

People, judged only by what the Architect already knows (the operator's chosen source, 2026-11-02): Opus 5.5 is the stronger model for multi-file reasoning and spotting subtle defects and costs several times more than Sonnet 5.5; Sonnet 5.5 is reliable on well-specified UI and route work. The operator's standing preference (2026-10-27) is Sonnet by default, Opus where a mistake is costly. No sample sizes: this source is general knowledge, not a measurement.
limits: The mock computes totals in the browser from a recording; the Hub route that must compute them over the whole filter within 2 seconds is not built or measured.
The mock's Hub-internals kinds are a sample (newest 200 of each); their totals in the app are not yet shown on real data.
Whether loop and job firing history records a run for each firing is not yet checked.
The run entry points (FR-10 to FR-12) and the Settings link were not part of the mock.
The acceptance criteria are proposed coverage; none has run.

The people were not judged against this project's per-model record or any current external comparison; the operator chose prior knowledge only, so how each model actually performs on this codebase is not reflected.

open_questions.question: Where it lives. Operator 2026-11-02, after driving the mock: inside Activity, as a fourth view beside Ledger, Activity and Logs.
Where the Hub's own traces go. Operator 2026-11-02, after driving the mock: behind a quieter 'Hub internals' choice, not beside agent runs.
A task with no reference. Operator 2026-11-02: shown by its title; a task that no longer exists is named as such, never by its raw id (six such tasks on the operator's Hub).
What counts as an error. Operator 2026-11-02: failed, plus cancelled or interrupted (stopped), plus a trace ended in error; not a failed tool call inside a completed run.
Unpriced runs. Operator 2026-11-02: shown as unpriced, never as zero.
The Settings 'Recent traces' list. Operator 2026-11-02: replaced by a link to the view.
Which statistics. Operator 2026-11-02: cost, duration and errors are what they want to see most; the others (tokens, call counts, waits) matter too but come second.
Which groupings. Operator 2026-11-02: switchable (between agent, model, task, conversation, kind, day).
Default contents. Operator 2026-11-02: agents' runs by default.
Size. Operator 2026-11-02 left it to the Architect: small.
Already built. Operator 2026-11-02: none of it is built.

problem: The operator finds the trace drawer good but 'not quite', and hard to reach: it opens only after a run, from a faint 'trace' link beside 'fold' above each turn (AgentTimeline.tsx:487-496) or from a run row in a task's story (TaskStory.tsx:344, inside the task detail drawer), and shows one run at a time. The conversation menu declares a 'Trace of the last turn' item (ConversationBar.tsx:201) that no caller wires up, so it never appears. The only list of traces is a ten-row panel inside Project Settings → Traces (TracesSection.tsx:319), mixed in with retention, OTLP export and clearing, and filtered by kind only. The Hub's list route already filters by run, task and conversation (hub/hub/api/v1/traces.py:41-75), but nothing on screen uses those filters, and the route has no agent or time-range filter. Nothing groups traces or gives statistics over them, so questions like 'what did this agent cost this week' or 'which runs failed' have no answer on screen. Most of the 136,761 recorded spans on the operator's Hub (2026-11-02) are the Hub's own git commands (58k) and requests (32k); about 1,170 traces are agent runs, and those are what the operator wants to see first.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02, after driving the mock: 'lives inside Activity'.
requirements.statement: The Activity tab has a Traces view for the selected project, beside Ledger, Activity and Logs, which the operator reaches without going through Settings.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: agents by default, and the Hub's internals behind a quieter choice. About 1,170 of the operator's traces are runs, beside tens of thousands of the Hub's own; unfiltered, the runs are buried.
requirements.statement: The traces view opens showing agents' runs only. The Hub's own traces (worker calls, requests, background work, events) are reached through a separate 'Hub internals' choice that is less prominent than the filters on runs, and appear only once one of them is chosen.
The traces view can be filtered by agent, conversation, task, run, kind and time range, any of them together, and the list and the statistics both show only what matches every filter in force.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02. Six tasks behind runs on the operator's Hub no longer exist; the mock showed one as 'task-b9bf0f35c2c5'.
requirements.statement: Each listed run shows its agent, model, task (its reference and title, when it worked one) or the conversation it was a turn of, when it started, how long it took, what it cost, and whether it counts as an error. A task with no reference and no title is shown as a task that no longer exists, never by its raw id.
The filtered traces can be grouped by agent, model, task, conversation, kind or day, switchable from the view, and each group shows how many traces it holds and its statistics.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: cost, duration and errors are what they want to see most; cancelled and interrupted runs count as errors, routine failed tool calls inside a finished run do not. On the operator's Hub runs are completed 1,211, failed 12, stopped 5, running 3.
requirements.statement: The view shows, over everything the current filter matches and for each group, the total cost, the total and average duration, and the number of errors, and these three are shown before any other statistic. A run counts as an error when it failed, when it was stopped (cancelled or interrupted), or when its trace ended in error; a run that completed with a failed tool call inside it does not.
The view also offers, less prominently, token counts, the number of model calls and tool calls, and time spent waiting for a permission or an answer, over the same filter and groups.

requirements.rationale: The list is paged (the Settings list shows 10 at a time); totals over one page would understate cost and errors without saying so.
requirements.statement: The statistics count every trace the filter matches, not only the page of rows currently loaded.

requirements.rationale: Driving the mock, a click in the middle of a row landed on its task and filtered instead of opening the run.
requirements.statement: Choosing a listed trace opens it in the existing trace view, and closing it returns to the traces view with the same filters and grouping. Narrowing to a row's task or conversation is a control of its own, so choosing the row anywhere else opens its trace.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: check every screen a trace can be reached from; the task story's run row already does this and is the model.
requirements.statement: Every screen that names or lists a specific agent run offers that run's trace, and following it opens that run's trace, not another run's or a list.

requirements.rationale: The per-turn link is faint and the 'Trace of the last turn' menu item exists but is never shown (ConversationBar.tsx:201).
requirements.statement: From a conversation, the operator opens the trace of its most recent run from the conversation's own controls, without finding the per-turn link, and each turn's own trace link stays.
A run count shown elsewhere (a build's runs, a task's runs, the project's work summary) opens the traces view filtered to exactly those runs.
On the operator's Hub (about 137k spans, 1,170 runs on 2026-11-02), the traces view's default list and statistics appear within 2 seconds.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02. 16 finished runs on the operator's Hub have no measured cost; counting them as zero would make a total look complete when it is not. The project's model record already reports them this way. A running run has not reported its cost yet, which is not the same as the Hub failing to measure it (found driving the mock).
requirements.statement: A finished run whose cost the Hub could not measure is shown as unpriced, never as a zero cost, and a cost total that leaves such runs out says how many it left out. A run still running is shown with no cost yet and is not counted as unpriced.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: one place to look for traces.
requirements.statement: Project Settings' traces section no longer lists traces itself; in place of its 'Recent traces' list it links to the traces view in Activity. Retention, export to a collector, download and clearing stay where they are.

in_scope: A traces view inside the Activity tab, beside Ledger, Activity and Logs, reachable without going through Settings.
Agents' runs shown by default; the Hub's own worker calls, requests, background work and events reachable through a separate, quieter 'Hub internals' choice.
Filtering traces by agent, conversation, task, run, kind and time range, in combination.
Grouping the filtered traces, switchable between agent, model, task, conversation, kind and day.
Statistics over the traces the current filter shows: cost, duration and errors foremost; tokens, model and tool call counts and waiting time available but secondary. Unpriced runs shown as unpriced.
Opening any listed trace in the existing run trace view.

Every screen that shows a specific run opening that run's trace: checking the existing entry points (a conversation turn, a task's story) and the dead 'Trace of the last turn' menu item, and making the conversation's entry point easy to find.
Replacing the Settings 'Recent traces' list with a link to the view.
non_goals: A trace of a whole conversation (slice 'conversation-trace').
Trace retention, OTLP export, download and clearing; they stay in Project Settings.
What the Hub records as spans.
Changes to the single-run trace drawer itself (waterfall and span detail); only a way for a list to open and close it.
Checkpoints (slices 'checkpoints-you-can-read' and 'start-from-a-checkpoint'); their entry points are covered there.
A top-bar tab of its own for traces (shown in the mock, not chosen).

summary: The first slice built of 'Checkpoints and traces you can find and use' (operator, 2026-11-02: traces first). Traces get a view of their own inside Activity, beside Ledger, Activity and Logs, showing agents' runs by default, with the Hub's own traces behind a quieter 'Hub internals' choice. The operator filters them by agent, conversation, task, run and time range, switches between groupings, and reads statistics over what is shown, with cost, duration and errors foremost. Every screen that shows a specific run opens that run's trace, and the Settings list gives way to a link to the view. The design was settled in a mock the operator drove on 2026-11-02 (hub/ui/mock, #traces).

tasks.description: audit-run-mentions names 'loop and job firing history where a firing has a run'. TVFGS-4 left it out, saying the firing record names no run. But JobRun carries conversation_id (models.py JobRun.conversation_id), and the Hub already pairs a firing with its run: scheduler.py:3524 finalize_job_run_for_conversation flips the firing when that run ends, and the firing's InboundQueueEntry carries delivered_in_run_id. Expose the run a firing started on GET /jobs/{id}/history (e.g. run_id, from the delivered entry or the conversation's run started at or after fired_at). Then give RunHistory (hub/ui/src/components/jobs/JobDetails.tsx) and the loop firing rows (LoopFiringGroup.tsx) a trace link that opens that run's trace. A firing with no run (skipped, refused) shows none. Write a Hub test that fails when the history's order is reversed, and a UI test per entry point.

tasks.description: GET /projects/{id}/traces/totals (hub/hub/traces.py trace_totals, ~line 2205) takes 2.6-4.0 s on a backup-API copy of the operator's database for proj-d85a82bf4216 (default and group_by=agent, operation=invoke_agent), while the list returns in ~0.1 s. Make the default statistics (and group_by=agent) return within 2 s on that copy under ordinary machine load: e.g. avoid re-running the _roots subquery once per auxiliary table (turn_usage, runs, chat/execute_tool counts, waits), avoid JSON-attribute extraction over every root span where a column or index would do, and check EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for full scans of trace_spans. Record timings (several calls, with CPU load noted) as FR-13 evidence.
